text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks, logging only non-blocking suggestions. This lets us measure real-world impact without disrupting teams. The trade-off is delayed feedback loops, but we gain unbiased data to decide if full deployment is worth the risk.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode trains reviewers to dismiss *all* autofeedback as noise, not just false positives—once merged PRs carry unaddressed suggestions, teams learn to ignore the tool entirely. A better test is running PR-Agent on *open* PRs only, with a visible "shadow mode" badge so reviewers know suggestions are experimental and not yet actionable. Settle it by measuring reviewer engagement: if the badge increases discussion of suggestions, the risk is real; if it drops, the alternative works.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs only, with a visible "shadow mode" badge so reviewers know suggestions are experimental—this cuts merged-PR noise while still measuring real impact. Add a weekly digest of suggestions sent to maintainers to keep the tool top-of-mind without manual log reviews.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs only, with a visible "shadow mode" badge and a weekly digest of suggestions sent to maintainers. This keeps the tool visible without polluting merged PRs, so reviewers don’t learn to ignore it. The trade-off is missing data on merged PRs, but we gain actionable feedback loops and maintain trust in the tool’s reliability.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs only, with a visible "shadow mode" badge and a weekly digest of suggestions sent to maintainers for two weeks.

Result: A clear measure of PR-Agent’s real-world impact on open PRs without polluting merged PRs or training reviewers to ignore it. Owned by Overhaul.
